children.text: The oldest city in the Philippines, where the cross planted by Magellan in

, the Basilica of Santo Niño, and Fort San Pedro all sit within the same neighborhood. A day or two is enough to fully enjoy a historical walk through the old town, crispy lechon, and night views from the Busay hills.
Cebu City is the center of Metro Cebu, the Philippines' second-largest metropolitan area, and the place where Spain first set foot in the Philippines. In
, Ferdinand Magellan landed here and baptized Rajah Humabon and his wife, and in
Miguel López de Legazpi founded Spain's first settlement. For this, Cebu is called the 'cradle of Philippine Catholicism' and the 'Queen City of the South.'

For travelers, the heart of Cebu City is its walkable old town. Magellan's Cross, the Basilica of Santo Niño, Cebu Metropolitan Cathedral, and Fort San Pedro — the Philippines' oldest and smallest triangular fort — all lie within a
1km

radius. A little further, the Parian district holds the 1730 Jesuit House, a wooden mansion once home to Spanish-era Chinese merchants, the Yap-Sandiego Ancestral House, and Casa Gorordo Museum, which shows life in the colonial era.

The city has another face too: modern business districts. IT Park and Cebu Business Park (around Ayala Center Cebu) and the SM Seaside area are packed with malls, cafes, and restaurants, while up in the Busay hills, Tops Lookout, the Taoist Temple, and Temple of Leah offer sweeping views of the city and the Mactan Channel.

Most Cebu travelers head straight to the Mactan resorts or the southern beaches (Moalboal, Oslob), but investing even just one day in the city lets you properly experience the starting point of Philippine history and Visayan food culture. It's especially recommended for history buffs, foodies, and families who need a backup plan for a rainy day.
The city covers about 315 km² and had about 960,000 residents as of

; Metro Cebu, which includes the surrounding cities, has more than 3 million. Colon Street is considered the oldest road in the Philippines, and Cebu Port is the country's second-largest port. The buildings of the old town carry clear dates. The current Basilica of Santo Niño was begun in
and completed in
, and in
Pope Paul VI elevated it to a minor basilica. The
October 2013
earthquake badly damaged its bell tower and façade, and they were restored by
. The octagonal pavilion housing Magellan's Cross was built around
, and the tindalo-wood cross that encases the original dates from
. The bell tower of Cebu Metropolitan Cathedral was also built in
and survived the Allied bombing of
, while the main church was rebuilt in the 1950s.
A cross covered in tindalo wood to protect the original cross Magellan planted in
is enshrined inside an octagonal pavilion, and the ceiling bears a painting of the baptism of Rajah Humabon and his wife. Entry to the plaza is free. However, there are reports that after the
September 2025

earthquake the pavilion developed cracks, so visitors were kept from going inside and instead paid their respects from outside or offered candles through the entrance and windows. Check before your visit whether you can currently enter the pavilion.
The oldest church in the Philippines, enshrining the 'Santo Niño' image of the Child Jesus that a Spanish expedition found in a burned village in
. On Fridays and Sundays, an endless procession of worshippers carrying candles files through.
A triangular fort first built by Legazpi as a wooden stockade in
and rebuilt in coral stone in
, with three bastions (La Concepción, Ignacio de Loyola, and San Miguel). The walls are about
6m
high and you can walk along the top for views over the old harbor; inside are a small museum displaying Spanish-era documents and cannons, and a courtyard. Admission has been reported as
for adults and
for students and seniors, though some guides list
, and opening hours are around
8 AM–7 PM
. Some accounts say it was damaged by the
September 2025
earthquake and is under repair, so check the latest announcements.

blocks.title: Walk through the Parian heritage district

children.text: Touring the 1730 Jesuit House, Yap-Sandiego Ancestral House, and Casa Gorordo Museum together shows you the life of old Cebu, a blend of Spanish, Chinese, and Filipino culture. The Heritage of Cebu Monument is also nearby.

Cebu lechon is famous for being stuffed with lemongrass and spices, making it delicious without any sauce. Order it by the quarter kilo at an old, established lechon shop at lunchtime, when the skin is crispiest.
A viewpoint about
above sea level in the Busay hills; go up at dusk and lights spread out over Cebu City, Mactan, and even across the sea toward Bohol.
A Chinese-style temple on the hill of the upscale Beverly Hills subdivision, with a dragon-decorated stairway, a pond, and good views of the city. Admission is free, but avoid revealing clothing.

blocks.title: Explore Carbon Market and local markets

children.text: Cebu's oldest and largest traditional market, where you can buy mangoes, dried fish, and fruit cheaply. Pickpockets are common, so carry your bag in front of you.

On rainy days, cut back the walking sections in the old town and switch to indoor attractions such as the Casa Gorordo Museum and the 1730 Jesuit House, plus the Ayala Center Cebu and SM Seaside malls.
National Museum of the Philippines – Cebu, next to Plaza Independencia — housed in a 1910 customs building; admission is free and it is closed on Mondays

Take a taxi to Ayala Center Cebu for shopping and dinner
The National Museum (closed Mondays) and Casa Gorordo (closed Sundays) have different days off, so to see both you need to plan your visit for Tuesday–Saturday.
Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB) is on Mactan Island, with daily direct flights from Korean cities like Incheon and Busan (about
4 hours 30 minutes
). From Manila it's about
1 hour 20 minutes
, with dozens of daily flights on Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific. From the airport to Cebu City's old town by taxi takes about
40 minutes–1 hour 30 minutes
depending on traffic, with fares around
. Using Grab is convenient since the fare is fixed in advance; the airport's official (yellow) taxis have a higher base fare than the white taxis.
If you have little luggage and want to save money, you can take MyBus, an air-conditioned airport bus that departs from in front of Terminals 1 and 2, to SM City Cebu. The fare is about
, the trip takes about
1 hour
depending on traffic, and buses run frequently between around
7 AM and 9 PM
. Check the airport information for the timetable.
Large ferries run from Manila to Cebu, taking about
20–24 hours
. Fastcraft from nearby islands like Bohol (Tagbilaran), Dumaguete, and Leyte arrive at Cebu's Pier 1, Pier 4, and others; from Bohol it takes about
2 hours
Taxis and Grab are the most convenient, at about
between the old town and IT Park. Jeepneys are cheap at about
but the routes are confusing. Traffic is heavy around Osmeña Boulevard and Mango Avenue between
5 and 8 PM
, so allow plenty of travel time. The attractions in the old town are
5–15 minutes
from each other on foot.
From
March 13, 2026

, Phase 1 of the Cebu BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) began partial service. It runs from SRP (Il Corso and SM Seaside) via the South Bus Terminal, Fuente Osmeña, the Capitol, and the Ayala Center area to IT Park, with a base fare of about
. It sometimes runs free during commuting hours (
6–9 AM
and
5–8 PM
), but sections, fares, and free hours may change, so check the latest announcements.

items.title: Airport terminals and getting here from Korea

children.text: Mactan-Cebu International Airport has two terminals. Terminal 1 handles domestic flights such as Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific, and AirAsia, and Terminal 2 handles international flights such as Korean Air. The two buildings stand side by side and are
5–10 minutes
apart on foot along a covered walkway, even with luggage, or you can take the free shuttle that runs 24 hours (about every
10–15 minutes
). The two terminals are not connected inside the security zone, so if you are transferring you must go outside.
From Incheon, Korean Air, Jeju Air, Jin Air, and Cebu Pacific operate direct flights, taking about
4 hours 30 minutes
. Airlines and flight counts change each season, so check before booking. The MyBus airport bus goes from Terminal 1 toward SM City Cebu, Ayala Center, and IT Park. The fare is about
and departures are listed at
30 minutes–1 hour
intervals, but the timetable changes often.
2GO Travel runs passenger ferries between Manila and Cebu Pier 1 two to three times a week (for example departing Sunday morning and Wednesday night), taking about
24 hours
each trip. Fares range from about
for the seat-type Mega Value Class to about
or more for a two-person State Room. The boarding check-in counter opens
4 hours
before departure and the gate closes
1 hour
before. Days and times can change, so check the latest timetable when you book. For travelers short on time, flying is far more practical.

items.title: From Cebu Port (Pier 1) to Bohol, Ormoc, and Siquijor

children.text: Most fastcraft to the nearby islands depart from Cebu Pier 1. To Bohol (Tagbilaran), OceanJet and SuperCat run at
30 minutes–1 hour
intervals, taking about
2 hours
, and regular seats are around
. Boats to Leyte (Ormoc), Dumaguete, Siquijor (Larena), and Camotes also leave from the same pier. A port fee of about
is charged separately, and OceanJet advises arriving
30 minutes
before departure, while Cokaliong Shipping advises
2 hours
before.
The dry season from
December
to
May
is good for traveling.
December–February
is relatively cool, while
March–May
is very hot, making midday walking tours tough, so plan your movement around the morning and late afternoon.
June–November

is the rainy season with frequent afternoon showers, though Cebu tends to be less affected by typhoons than eastern parts of the Philippines. Still, there have been cases of serious damage, such as Typhoon Odette (Rai) in
, so check weather forecasts during the rainy season.
The biggest event is the Sinulog Festival, held every third Sunday of
January

. Street parades and dance competitions honoring the Santo Niño take place, and the whole city is in a festive mood for about a week before and after. Accommodation prices rise sharply and traffic is restricted during this period, so book months in advance. Holy Week before Easter also brings many church events.
On
November 4, 2025

, Typhoon Tino (Kalmaegi) dumped record-breaking rain on Cebu; flash floods submerged much of Metro Cebu, and more than 130 people died in Cebu Province alone. If a typhoon warning is issued in the late rainy season,
October–November
, avoid traveling along rivers and low-lying areas, and leave some buffer in your schedule the day before you fly home in case flights or ferries are canceled.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
If sightseeing is your goal, IT Park (Lahug) or around Ayala Center Cebu is safe and convenient, with plenty of restaurants. Business hotels run about
a night, and luxury hotels

or more. Near the old town (around Colon Street) is cheap but quiet and less safe at night, so it's not recommended for first-time visitors. Staying at a Mactan resort and visiting downtown as a day trip is also a common approach.

The signature of Cebu's food is lechon. Long-established lechon shops around Lahug and Mandaue (Rico's Lechon, CnT Lechon, Zubuchon, and others) are famous among travelers, and Zubuchon is known for Anthony Bourdain's praise of it as the best pig in the world. Most open at
6–8 AM
and sell through the morning, so popular shops are reported to sell out by

on weekends. The Larsian barbecue alley near Fuente Osmeña is Cebu's late-night food spot where you pick skewers and have them grilled, and the Cebu-style way is to pair them with pusô, rice cooked in small woven pouches. Street food includes pungko-pungko, which sells fried chicken and pork, and for dessert dried mango and otap pastries are famous and make good gifts.
Larsian closed during COVID-19, and in
September 2023
the provincial government renovated it and reopened it under the name Sugbo Sentro. Locals still call it Larsian, and it is open
10 AM to midnight
. The provincial government is pushing a renovation to bring back the old name and atmosphere, so the mix of stalls may change.
Carbon Market, running since the
19th century

, is the oldest market in Central Visayas, and its name is said to come from its location near the coal (Spanish carbón) yard of the old Cebu railway. Seafood, dried fish, fruit, vegetables, and secondhand clothing stalls are all jumbled together, and fresh goods are best from dawn until
7 AM
. There are also reports of a night market on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from
. Bargaining is expected and many stalls take cash only. Pickpockets are frequent, so carry your belongings in front of you.
The Basilica of Santo Niño and the Metropolitan Cathedral may restrict entry for sleeveless tops or short shorts, so bring clothing that covers your shoulders.
Installing the Grab app spares you the stress of haggling over taxi fares. During rush hour, cars can take a while to be assigned, so allow extra time.
The old town has little shade, so start early in the morning and schedule museums or indoor activities for midday.
Public transport to Tops Lookout is inconvenient, so charter a round-trip taxi or use a habal-habal. It's recommended to leave
1 hour
before sunset.
Lechon is roasted in the morning and sold at lunch, so by late afternoon the skin may have gone soft or it may have sold out.
It's safer to withdraw cash from bank ATMs inside shopping malls. Standalone street ATMs carry a skimming risk.
International departures at Cebu Mactan Airport often take a long time to process, so arrive
3 hours
before your flight.

. The lookout is open
24 hours

The Sinulog grand parade is held on the third Sunday of January every year. On
January 18, 2026
, a reported 3 million people watched the parade and about 5.2 million came out for the festival as a whole; in
it falls on
January 17
. The parade starts in the morning and roads are closed, so book accommodation within walking distance.
Pickpocketing and snatch theft are common around Carbon Market, Colon Street, and the Basilica of Santo Niño. Don't walk around holding your phone in your hand.
In front of the church, people may pressure you to buy candles or souvenirs, or ask for money by offering to 'pray for you' — politely decline.
Don't take taxis that won't turn on the meter or that demand a flat fare — use Grab instead.
Midday temperatures often exceed 33°C, so watch out for dehydration and heatstroke, and drink water frequently.
During the Sinulog Festival, the crowds are enormous, and lost valuables and separated children are common.
After the magnitude 6.9 earthquake on
September 30, 2025

(epicenter in Bogo, in the north), heritage sites in Cebu City, including Fort San Pedro, were damaged or closed to visitors for a time for inspection. There are reports that the Magellan's Cross pavilion was also cracked and allowed only prayer from outside, so check before you go that any site on your itinerary is open, and prepare an alternative plan.
Traffic congestion in Cebu City is severe. On the day you head to the airport, allow twice your usual travel time.
